desc: The demesne of Limgrave, far south of the Erdtree, is bordered to the northwest by the cliffs of Stormveil, and under its ever-clouded skies roll the great steppes of the pale lands.
whatItIs: The first region a new character enters, a wide-open steppe far south of the Erdtree with the cliffs of Stormveil rising to the northwest. Skies stay perpetually overcast and the terrain rolls in gentle waves, offering room to learn movement and combat at a low-stakes pace.
whyItMatters: The region introduces core systems like Site of Grace checkpoints, leveling, and NPC interactions while keeping enemy pressure manageable. Stormveil Castle anchors the northern edge, and Godrick the Grafted serves as a natural benchmark for whether a build is ready to push further.
whenToUse: Start here the moment the game loads, with no preparation needed. The enemies are slow enough to read their attack patterns, and the open layout lets a character rest at any grace without backtracking. Move on once the shardbearer falls or the early-tier foes stop posing a challenge.
name: Limgrave

desc: The peninsula, to Limgrave's south, is named for its unceasing rainfall, redolent of lament.
whatItIs: A narrow stretch of coastal land jutting south from Limgrave, drenched in unceasing rain that muffles every sound. Paths tighten, enemy aggression steps up, and the constant downpour turns every engagement into a slightly closer exchange than the open steppe before it.
whyItMatters: The region acts as a difficulty bridge between the forgiving opening area and the more demanding lands that follow. Several early side quests route through these rain-soaked paths, and the enemy variety expands beyond basic soldiers into new types that test a build's range of defenses.
whenToUse: Visit right after finishing Limgrave, while gear is still basic and the character's level is low. The enemies hit harder and faster than anything in the steppe, so stock up on healing flasks and be ready to dodge more often.
name: Weeping Peninsula

desc: The majority of Liurnia, known for its vast forests and ever-present fog, is sinking into a lake.
whatItIs: Fog hangs over vast forests that are slowly sinking into a lake, giving the whole region a drowned, otherworldly quality. Visibility drops in the mist, and the terrain shifts between tall tree lines and open water crossings that force careful navigation.
whyItMatters: Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon, guards the Academy of Raya Lucaria at the region's heart, and the area is a primary source of early sorcery spells and magic-focused gear. The fog also changes how combat plays out, since enemies can appear from unexpected angles behind mist.
whenToUse: Enter once the character has some magic or faith investment, since the local enemies lean heavily on elemental attacks. A few levels above the previous region's challenges and a decent armor set make the fog crossings considerably less punishing.
name: Liurnia of the Lakes

desc: Caelid, known as the locale of the last battle between General Radahn and Malenia, Blade of Miquella, is a vast land consummately marred by scarlet rot.
whatItIs: A vast scarlet-rotted landscape, the site of the last battle between General Radahn and Malenia, Blade of Miquella. The ground is stained red, enemies carry aggressive bleed and rot effects, and the overall atmosphere is one of decay and violence.
whyItMatters: Starscourge Radahn, a shardbearer boss, is fought at Redmane Castle within this region, making it a defining encounter in the base game. The region also rewards exploration with powerful late-game weapons and upgrade materials that are unavailable in earlier zones.
whenToUse: Approach only when the character is well into the mid-game, with strong resistances against bleed and rot. A higher level, upgraded gear, and healing that counters rot are all wise to have before stepping into the red landscape.
name: Caelid

desc: The dragons that escaped the scarlet rot and made nest of the plateau to Caelid's north. Thus it was named "Dragonbarrow," and none dare to enter.
whatItIs: North of Caelid, a plateau where dragons escaped the scarlet rot and made their nests. The air is thick with ash and the skeletal remains of ancient wyrms line the ridgelines, giving the zone a desolate, prehistoric feel.
whyItMatters: Dragon-slaying here yields powerful drops, and the region's enemies are built around aerial pressure and fire breath. It pairs with Caelid as a companion zone, offering a different flavor of combat alongside the rot-soaked plains.
whenToUse: Tackle it alongside or just after Caelid, when the character can handle sustained aerial attacks and fire damage. Bringing a fire-resistant armor set and a weapon that can reach mounted enemies makes the dragon fights considerably less stressful.
name: Greyoll's Dragonbarrow

whatItIs: Highland grass and scattered ruins define this zone, which sits between the lowland areas and the volcanic peaks to the north. The terrain is open and bright, a sharp contrast to the rot and fog of the neighboring regions below.
whyItMatters: The plateau is the crossroads between Leyndell to the east and Mt. Gelmir to the south, so most players pass through it on the way to both. Several upgrade materials and side quest markers cluster here, making it a productive stop before heading toward the capital or the volcano.
whenToUse: Visit after clearing the regions below, when the character has a solid weapon and some mid-tier upgrades. The enemies use more aggressive melee patterns than the opening areas, so a character with decent poise and a reliable dodge is well matched.
name: Altus Plateau

desc: Mt. Gelmir, which houses the Volcano Manor at its summit, is characterized by sheer cliffs and ominous skies. These qualities only became more pronounced after the Shattering.
whatItIs: Sheer cliffs and ominous skies define this volcanic peak, where the Volcano Manor sits at the summit. The landscape is dark, ash-choked, and built around vertical traversal up narrow stone faces.
whyItMatters: The Volcano Manor at the top hosts a network of mercenary NPCs and a raid boss, making it one of the more densely packed zones in the base game. Volcanic-themed weapons and upgrade materials are found here, along with quest content that pays out in powerful gear.
whenToUse: Approach once the character can handle fire-based attacks and has a reliable way to reach the summit. The enemies are fast and aggressive, so a build with good mobility and a weapon that builds bleed or poise break works well.
name: Mt. Gelmir

desc: Journey to the capital Leyndell, to the east of the Altus Plateau, at the foot of the Erdtree. The Two Fingers will deny your passage no longer. You may be our best hope. Find your way to the Elden Ring.
whatItIs: The capital city at the foot of the Erdtree, to the east of the Altus Plateau. Its grand architecture and open plazas give it a regal feel, but the streets are patrolled by elite soldiers and the air hums with forbidden magic.
whyItMatters: It gates access to the Mountaintops of the Giants and the Consecrated Snowfield beyond, making it a mandatory waypoint on the main path. Key NPCs, major questlines, and a shardbearer boss all converge here, so it is a hub for endgame progression.
whenToUse: Enter when the character is solidly in the mid-to-late game range, with upgraded equipment and at least one strong weapon art. The enemies use coordinated attacks and magic, so a build that can handle pressure from multiple angles is ideal.
name: Leyndell, Royal Capital
aliases: Crumbling Farum Azula & Leyndell, Ashen Capital

whatItIs: A frozen alpine zone of sheer stone faces and howling winds, reached after passing through Leyndell. The air is thin, the paths are narrow, and giant architecture looms over every trail.
whyItMatters: The region is home to the Fire Giant, a massive late-game boss guarding the way to burn the Erdtree, along with several other challenges that test a build's raw power and mechanical skill. Upgrade materials found here are valuable, and the area's enemies hit with crushing force that demands poise-breaking tools.
whenToUse: Save it for the latter portion of a playthrough, once the character has strong poise-breaking tools and can deal with frost damage. A weapon that scales with Dexterity or Faith and a talisman that boosts damage help against the heavily armored foes.
name: Mountaintops of the Giants
aliases: Mountaintops of the Giants & Flame Peak

desc: The route through this land, crossed east to west by a frozen river, leads to Miquella's Haligtree. This is the path taken by those unchosen, though it is a trial all the same.
whatItIs: Bleak and wind-scoured, the frozen expanse is crossed east to west by a river of ice and leads directly to Miquella's Haligtree. There is very little cover, and the enemies strike with cold, deliberate precision.
whyItMatters: It serves as the approach to Miquella's Haligtree, one of the most significant endgame destinations in the base game. The enemies here are punishing to fight, and the lack of nearby grace points means each engagement demands near-perfect execution.
whenToUse: Treat it as a late-game challenge, entering only when the character is at a high level with a fully upgraded weapon and strong resistances. A well-stocked set of flasks and a build that can sustain damage through extended exchanges makes the difference.
name: Consecrated Snowfield

whatItIs: An ancient city caught in a loop of time, its streets and arenas repeating in an endless cycle. The architecture is grand but decaying, and the inhabitants behave as if the same day plays over and over.
whyItMatters: It is home to one of the most iconic boss fights in the game and offers unique rewards that cannot be obtained anywhere else. Its self-contained loop makes it a natural destination for a focused, high-difficulty challenge rather than a farming ground.
whenToUse: Visit when the character is at the higher end of their power, with a weapon suited to the specific boss mechanics and enough healing to survive extended fights. It is not a zone for exploration; it is a destination with a clear goal and a clear exit.
name: Crumbling Farum Azula

whatItIs: The central hub where Tarnished gather, a warm and lively contrast to the hostile wilderness outside. NPCs offer quests, trade items, and share lore, while a fireplace and bed provide a safe resting point.
whyItMatters: It is the primary social and quest hub for the entire playthrough, where most major questlines are triggered and where items are bought and sold. Returning here between excursions is how a character tracks progress and picks up new objectives.
whenToUse: Stop by whenever a quest needs to be accepted or a new item needs to be purchased. It is always safe, always accessible, and the right place to sort through inventory or speak with an NPC before heading back out.
name: Roundtable Hold

whatItIs: Beneath the surface, a dark waterway winds through underground channels, its banks lined with the remains of ancient civilizations. The atmosphere is quiet and funereal, with enemies that move slowly but hit with surprising force.
whyItMatters: The river serves as a gateway to deeper underground content and connects several major subterranean zones. Certain questlines and hidden areas are only accessible by following its current, making it a key corridor rather than a destination in itself.
whenToUse: Enter when the character has a way to navigate dark, enclosed spaces and can handle enemies that use water-based attacks. A light source and a weapon with good reach make the narrow channels much more comfortable to traverse.
name: Siofra River

desc: Descend underground where the fallen star struck Limgrave. And make it yours. The precious treasure of Nokron.
whatItIs: An underground city buried where a fallen star struck Limgrave, its architecture alien and its treasures hoarded beyond easy reach. The air is still and the light is faint, giving the whole place a sealed, forgotten quality.
whyItMatters: It holds valuable early-game loot, including unique weapons and upgrade materials that are hard to find elsewhere. The enemies inside are aggressive and the layout is confusing, which is why the treasures remain unclaimed by many who pass by.
whenToUse: Visit once the character can handle enclosed combat and has a weapon that breaks poise effectively. The area is accessible from the surface world, but its rewards are best claimed with mid-tier gear and a few levels of buffer.
name: Nokron, Eternal City

whatItIs: Dark and still, the river flows through the deepest underground layers, its black water reflecting almost no light. The paths along its banks are narrow and the enemies that patrol them are unlike anything in the surface world.
whyItMatters: It acts as a corridor to some of the most significant endgame locations in the base game, including the Consecrated Snowfield. The enemies here are fast, numerous, and punish any wasted movement, so preparation matters more than raw stats.
whenToUse: Approach when the character has strong mobility and a reliable dodge, since the enemies close distance quickly. A weapon that builds a status effect or a bow for keeping pressure at range both work well in the tight channels.
name: Ainsel River

whatItIs: Tangled roots of ancient trees form a dense overhead canopy in this underground forest, filtering what little light reaches the ground. The air is thick with spores and the creatures that live here move in packs, attacking from multiple directions.
whyItMatters: The region is a hub for several late-game quests and houses a powerful boss that guards a key item. The enemies are aggressive and numerous, making it a zone that rewards preparation and area-of-effect tools over single-target brute force.
whenToUse: Enter when the character has a weapon with strong area effect or a status buildup that works against groups. A talisman that boosts stamina or a shield with good poise makes the pack fights much more manageable.
name: Deeproot Depths

desc: In the lightless depths lies the grave of an ancient civilization. It is here Mohg, the Lord of Blood, is building his palace, to be the seat of his coming dynasty named Mohgwyn. And whatever nightmares that may bring.
whatItIs: In the lightless depths, the palace of Mohg, the Lord of Blood, rises above the grave of an ancient civilization. The architecture is ornate and blood-stained, and the inhabitants serve a dynasty built on inherited power.
whyItMatters: The region is the seat of a major NPC questline and houses a shardbearer boss tied to the blood affinity. Unique weapons, spells, and talismans found here are unavailable anywhere else in the base game, making it a worthwhile detour for dedicated players.
whenToUse: Visit when the character has resisted to blood damage and carries a weapon that can break the specific guard patterns of the local elite enemies. The zone is best explored with a full set of mid-to-late game gear and a plan for the boss's mechanics.
name: Mohgwyn Palace

whatItIs: Vast fungal growths and twisted architecture fill this underground cavern, where the boundary between natural stone and built structure blurs. The air is damp and the enemies here use a mix of poison and physical attacks that demand varied defenses.
whyItMatters: It is closely tied to the Dung Eater's questline and holds a tough boss encounter along with several unique items connected to specific NPC quests. The area is more open than other underground zones, offering room for exploration and hidden paths that reward careful map-reading.
whenToUse: Approach with a build that resists poison and has a reliable way to break guard. The enemies are tough and the boss requires a specific approach, so a few extra levels and a well-chosen weapon make the difference between a fair fight and a losing one.
name: Subterranean Shunning-Grounds

desc: A somber plain covered in spiritgraves. The spiral tower of the Hornsent lies to the northwest, and the entire expanse is marred by the harrowing ravages of war.
whatItIs: Spiritgraves cover this somber plain, their fields marred by the harrowing ravages of war. The spiral tower of the Hornsent rises to the northwest, and the ground is littered with the debris of ancient battles.
whyItMatters: The region is the entry point to the central conflict of the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion, and its enemies introduce new mechanics not seen in the base game. Key items and progression gates are found throughout the spiritgrave fields, making it a mandatory zone for expansion content.
whenToUse: The Shadow of the Erdtree expansion is required to enter this area. Approach with a build suited to the expansion's enemy types, a weapon that can handle the new mechanics, and a solid set of resistances for the status effects introduced here.
name: Gravesite Plain

desc: A captivating vista of brilliant blue flowers, intermingled with colossal stone coffins of unknown origin that seemingly drifted to this place.
whatItIs: Brilliant blue flowers grow in dense clusters along this coastline, intermingled with colossal stone coffins of unknown origin that seem to have drifted to this place. The overall mood is one of serene mystery, a calm contrast to the war-torn plains nearby.
whyItMatters: Between the blue blooms and the fallen coffins sit weapons and gear that the base game never offers. Several enemy archetypes patrol the open paths here, each one introducing a combat pattern that later stretches of the shadow world will test again. A careful sweep of the region early on hands out tools that make everything past it feel less punishing.
whenToUse: Access to this zone requires the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion. Enter with a build that can handle the new status effects and a weapon suited to the local enemy patterns, and treat the coastal paths as a series of short, intense encounters.
name: Cerulean Coast

desc: To the east, the jagged peak thrusts upward into the clouds.
whatItIs: A towering peak that thrusts upward into the clouds on the eastern edge of the Shadow realm. It is a late-game region in the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion, reached after working through the earlier shadow areas.
whyItMatters: The ascent is lined with tough field enemies and challenging optional encounters that demand a fully developed build. The upper reaches hold high-tier loot and progression items that feed into the endgame of the expansion.
whenToUse: The Shadow of the Erdtree expansion must be owned before this area becomes available. Head here after clearing most of the other shadow regions, since the fights along the way expect a character with high-level equipment and a committed stat spread.
name: Jagged Peak
aliases: Foot of the Jagged Peak, Charo's Hidden Grave & Jagged Peak

desc: Scadu Altus is named after its counterpart in the realm of the Erdtree. At its center lies the shadow keep.
whatItIs: Scadu Altus is a vast open region in the Shadow realm, named after its counterpart near the Erdtree. At its center lies Shadow Keep, which anchors the area's main story progression.
whyItMatters: The altus connects multiple shadow regions and hosts several major encounters with high-value loot caches tucked along the routes. Clearing it opens the path to Shadow Keep and the areas beyond.
whenToUse: Access requires the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion. Approach it once the earlier shadow regions are mostly cleared, with a build that has enough level and gear to handle the stronger enemies scattered across the open field.
name: Scadu Altus

desc: To have his revenge on Sir Messmer, there is only one place he will go. The black keep.
whatItIs: Shadow Keep is a dark fortress at the center of Scadu Altus, built as the seat of power in the Shadow realm. It is where the character confronts Sir Messmer to exact the revenge that drives the expansion's story.
whyItMatters: Clearing the keep's interior rewards the character with high-tier gear and progression items that gate the end of the expansion. The corridors also hold optional challenges and lore fragments that flesh out the Shadow realm's history.
whenToUse: This area is part of the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion. Arrive with a fully upgraded build and strong talismans, since the fights inside are calibrated for a character who has already cleared the surrounding shadow regions.
name: Shadow Keep

desc: At the east of the Gravesite Plain. A thick forest sprawls at the depths of the ravine that is untouched even by sunlight. Known as the sanctum of Sage Midra, and is a region forbidden by the hornsent.
whatItIs: A dense forest sprawls at the bottom of a deep ravine east of the Gravesite Plain, where no sunlight reaches. It is known as the sanctum of Sage Midra, and the hornsent have forbidden entry to the area.
whyItMatters: The undergrowth is thick with aggressive enemy packs and hidden loot that rewards careful exploration. Because it sits deep in the ravine, it makes a natural late stop for sweeping out remaining content before pushing toward Shadow Keep.
whenToUse: The Shadow of the Erdtree expansion is a prerequisite for entry. Visit it after clearing the Gravesite Plain and most of the open shadow regions, with a build strong enough to handle the dense encounters in the dark.
name: Abyssal Woods

desc: These giant ruins are flooded, overgrown, and split into two by a chasm. To the southwest is the Church of the Bud, overlooking the tower of shadow.
whatItIs: Flooded and overgrown, these giant ruins are split into two halves by a wide chasm. To the southwest, the Church of the Bud sits overlooking the tower of shadow.
whyItMatters: The two halves hold different enemy layouts and loot, so crossing the chasm opens a second cluster of treasures worth searching. The area as a whole is a late-game exploration zone that fits between the open shadow regions and the push toward Shadow Keep.
whenToUse: Entry requires owning the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion. Work through it after clearing the surrounding open regions and before heading into Shadow Keep, since the enemy density here expects a character with solid stats and upgraded equipment.
name: Ancient Ruins of Rauh

desc: O tower of ours, hidden in shadow. O lofty spiral piercing the heavens. Lead him safely unto greater Godhood. And in divinity grant our salvation.
whatItIs: Enir-Ilim is a slender spiral tower that climbs through the shadow realm toward the upper sky. It belongs to the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion and shows up late in the campaign, well past the wide open fields. The tight winding interior rewards steady guard work and punishes any hasty leap between ledges.
whyItMatters: The climb up the spiral is a gauntlet of tight combat encounters and hidden passages, with high-value loot stashed at intervals along the way. Reaching the top yields rewards and progression that carry into the closing stretch of the expansion.
whenToUse: This area requires the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion to be installed first. Tackle the climb after the build is solid and talismans have seen a few upgrades, because the cramped passages leave little room for error and the foes inside land heavy hits.
name: Enir-Ilim
